topic: Post-graduation work permit eligibility
date_basis: Explicit application-date rule on current IRCC eligibility page
previous_rule: Archive coverage for this topic begins at this change; the archive does not yet reconstruct every earlier PGWP eligibility rule.
new_rule: For PGWP applications submitted on or after November 1, 2024, most applicants must meet a language requirement. For non-degree university and college/polytechnic/non-university graduates, a field-of-study requirement can apply when the study permit application was submitted on or after November 1, 2024. Bachelor's, master's and doctoral graduates have no field-of-study requirement. Flight-school graduates have specific exemptions.
transition_rule: IRCC states that applicants who submitted their PGWP application before November 1, 2024 do not need to meet the new language requirement; field-of-study rules depend on study-permit application date and program type.

topic: Family open work permits for spouses of international students
date_basis: IRCC notice expressly states effective January 21, 2025
previous_rule: From March 19, 2024 through January 20, 2025, family OWP eligibility for spouses and common-law partners of international students was already limited to master's/doctoral degree students, certain professional degree programs and select eligible pilots. The January 21, 2025 rule further narrowed the master's cohort to programs of at least 16 months and established the successor specified-program framework.
new_rule: From January 21, 2025, family OWP eligibility for international students was limited to spouses or common-law partners of students in specified programs, including master's programs of 16 months or longer, doctoral programs and select professional or eligible programs.
transition_rule: Previously approved unexpired permits remain valid. IRCC also preserves specified extension situations for in-Canada family members.

topic: Family open work permits for spouses of foreign workers
date_basis: IRCC notice expressly states effective January 21, 2025
previous_rule: Family OWP eligibility was broader before the January 21, 2025 restriction.
new_rule: For high-skilled workers outside specified permanent-residence pathways, eligible spouses or common-law partners are generally tied to principal applicants working in TEER 0 or 1 or selected TEER 2 or 3 occupations, with a general requirement that the principal applicant's work authorization remain valid for at least 16 months after IRCC receives the spouse's application. Dependent children ceased to qualify under this measure. Family members of low-skilled workers outside eligible pathways are generally not eligible under this measure.
transition_rule: Specified in-Canada extensions remain possible. Free-trade-agreement and permanent-residence-pathway cases have separate rules. Later targeted measures create additional exceptions.

topic: Express Entry CRS points for arranged employment
date_basis: Current Ministerial Instructions mark the relevant CRS provisions repealed March 25, 2025
previous_rule: Before March 25, 2025, qualifying job offers could add 50 or 200 CRS points depending on the occupation.
new_rule: As of March 25, 2025, Express Entry no longer awards CRS points for job offers. A valid job offer can still matter for eligibility under programs where arranged employment remains part of the program rules.
transition_rule: IRCC applied the removal to current and future candidates in the Express Entry pool.

topic: PGWP eligible field-of-study list
date_basis: IRCC notice says effective June 25, 2025
previous_rule: The field-of-study list in force immediately before June 25, 2025 applied to affected PGWP pathways.
new_rule: IRCC added 119 fields of study and removed 178 fields, reporting 920 eligible fields after the update.
transition_rule: Students who applied for a study permit before June 25, 2025 remained eligible if their field was on the list when they applied, even if it was removed on June 25.

topic: PGWP eligible field-of-study list
date_basis: IRCC states the eligible CIP codes were updated July 4, 2025
previous_rule: Between June 25 and July 3, 2025, the published list reflected the June 25 removals, subject to transition protection.
new_rule: On July 4, 2025, IRCC added back the fields of study that had been removed on June 25. IRCC states those restored fields remain eligible until the list is next updated.
transition_rule: IRCC states that applicants who submitted a study permit application in one of those fields between June 25 and July 4 still meet the field-of-study requirement when they graduate. The current IRCC field-of-study page also states the list is frozen for 2026.

topic: Express Entry category-based selection priorities
date_basis: Official backgrounder published February 18, 2026; no separate coming-into-force date is stated on that page
previous_rule: The 2025 category structure preceded the 2026 annual category update.
new_rule: For 2026, IRCC announced new categories for medical doctors with Canadian work experience, researchers with Canadian work experience, senior managers with Canadian work experience, transport occupations and skilled military recruits with a Canadian Armed Forces job offer. Renewed categories are French-language proficiency, health care and social services, education, STEM and trades. IRCC states the minimum work experience for all renewed occupation categories increased from six months to one year in an eligible occupation within the previous three years.
transition_rule: This entry records the official 2026 category announcement. Because the source does not state a separate effective date, the archive does not convert the publication date into a legal coming-into-force date.

topic: Open work permits for spouses of workers under an SIP agreement
date_basis: Current IRCC eligibility page expressly states as of March 23, 2026
previous_rule: This targeted SIP spouse eligibility did not apply before the stated March 23, 2026 start date.
new_rule: As of March 23, 2026, a spouse may apply for an open work permit when the principal applicant has a valid work permit or work-permit letter of introduction issued under an SIP agreement, is employed or has a job offer in an occupation at any TEER level, and is or will be living in Canada while employed. The usual 16-month validity requirement does not apply to this targeted measure.
transition_rule: Applicants must follow the specific IRCC instructions and documentary requirements for the measure.

topic: Open work permits for spouses of certain Quebec PSTQ temporary workers
date_basis: IRCC notice expressly states starting June 5, 2026 and measure remains open until end of 2026
previous_rule: A March 13, 2026 public policy supported specified Quebec temporary workers; the June 5 change expanded spouse/common-law-partner eligibility.
new_rule: Starting June 5, 2026, once the temporary foreign worker is found eligible under the public policy, a spouse or common-law partner can apply for an open work permit if they have valid temporary resident status in Canada or their status expired within the previous 90 days, and they are named on the principal applicant's permanent selection application under Quebec's Skilled Worker Selection Program.
transition_rule: The measure is time-limited through December 31, 2026, subject to the detailed eligibility rules on the current IRCC program pages.

topic: Short-term study without a study permit for valid work permit holders
date_basis: The temporary public policy was signed August 5, 2026 and states that it comes into effect 30 days after signature; IRCC's implementation page expressly states September 4, 2026. The policy expires December 31, 2027 unless revoked earlier.
previous_rule: Without this public policy, R188(1)(c) requires a qualifying course or program of studies of six months or less to be completed within the period of stay authorized upon entry into Canada.
new_rule: Eligible foreign nationals who hold a valid work permit may study without a study permit in a course or program lasting six months or less. The public policy exempts the R188(1)(c) requirement that the course or program be completed within the period of stay authorized upon entry. The exemption ends when the valid work permit expires or the public policy expires or is revoked, whichever occurs first.
transition_rule: The measure applies from September 4, 2026. The signed public policy states the eligibility condition as holding a valid work permit and does not state a separate historical work-permit-application cut-off. IRCC's operational page says a learning institution may ask for the valid work permit as proof of eligibility.

authority: Government of Saskatchewan, Saskatchewan Immigrant Nominee Program
topic: SINP 2026 capped-sector intake schedule
date_basis: Current SINP Processing Statistics and OASIS registration pages verified September 11, 2026 state that September 14-15 is the final 2026 capped-sector intake and that nomination spaces previously allocated for later intakes were moved into September. Neither current page states when this schedule change was first published or a separate change-effective date, so effective_from is left null.
previous_rule: The current official page itself confirms that nomination spaces had previously been allocated to later 2026 intakes. This archive does not reconstruct or assign an end date to that earlier schedule because the current official evidence does not state when the revised schedule was first published.
new_rule: SINP states that the final capped-sector intake for 2026 will occur on September 14 and 15. On September 14 at 9:30 a.m., Trucking has a 150-position limit and Retail has 175; Accommodation opens at 1:30 p.m. with 50 positions. Food Services opens September 15 at 1:30 p.m. with 175 positions. SINP states that nomination spaces previously allocated for later intakes will be made available in September.
transition_rule: For capped sectors, SINP states that employers can submit only during an active intake window and only for candidates with six months or less remaining on a valid work permit. Positions are first-come, first-served. The SINP OASIS registration page states that capped-sector EPAs submitted outside an active intake period, or for candidates whose work permits expire more than six months from the submission date, will be closed and returned.

topic: Manitoba Workforce Transition Bridge open work permit public policy
date_basis: The signed A25.2 public policy states that it comes into effect on the date it is signed and is dated July 6, 2026. It expires December 31, 2027 unless revoked earlier.
previous_rule: A previous temporary public policy facilitated work permits for prospective provincial nominee candidates. The 2026 Manitoba measure retains a defined cohort previously identified by Manitoba and creates its own current eligibility and exemption conditions.
new_rule: Eligible members of the defined Manitoba cohort may receive an open work permit if they meet one of the policy's status or work-authorization situations and provide a Manitoba support letter issued on or before December 31, 2025 confirming MPNP Expression of Interest placement on or before that date, plus a letter of employment from the current employer. The policy provides specified regulatory exemptions including R200(1)(c), and for the restoration cohort additional R182, R199 and R200(3)(e) exemptions.
transition_rule: The measure is limited to the defined Manitoba cohort and is not a general open work permit for all Manitoba workers. IRCC's operational page states the permit may be issued for up to two years and is not for applicants already nominated by a province or territory.

topic: 2023 temporary study-permit exemption for certain work permit holders
date_basis: IRCC's signed A25.2 public policy states it came into effect June 27, 2023 and expired June 27, 2026; it was dated May 30, 2023.
previous_rule: Before this measure, affected workers remained subject to the ordinary study-permit and R188 study-without-permit framework unless another exemption applied.
new_rule: Eligible foreign nationals could study without a study permit if they held a valid work permit whose associated application was received by IRCC on or before June 7, 2023, or had submitted a work-permit renewal on or before June 7, 2023 and were authorized to work under R186(u). The policy provided exemptions from R188(1)(a)-(d).
transition_rule: The exemption ended when the relevant pending renewal was refused, the work permit expired, or the public policy expired or was revoked, whichever came first. The policy expired June 27, 2026 and is preserved as historical state rather than treated as the same mechanism as the different September 2026 short-study policy.

topic: Construction-trade apprentices studying without a study permit
date_basis: Current IRCC operational page states the public policy starts February 26, 2025 and is open until February 26, 2027.
previous_rule: The archive does not assert an equivalent construction-apprentice study exemption before February 26, 2025.
new_rule: Eligible construction-trade apprentices may study without a study permit for apprenticeship study requirements when they have a valid work permit, have a job in an eligible construction occupation, and have an apprenticeship agreement registered with the relevant provincial or territorial apprenticeship and certification authority.
transition_rule: IRCC requires the eligibility conditions to be met when the exemption is requested and when a decision is made. The measure remains open until February 26, 2027; detailed proof and authorization instructions remain controlled by the current IRCC operational pages.

topic: Quebec PSTQ prospective permanent residence work-permit public policy
date_basis: The archived IRCC public policy states that it came into effect March 13, 2026. The June 5, 2026 successor expressly revokes and replaces the policy signed March 12, so this archive bounds the predecessor's active state through June 4, 2026.
previous_rule: The archive does not yet reconstruct a directly equivalent Quebec PSTQ work-permit public policy before March 13, 2026.
new_rule: The policy facilitated employer-specific IMP work permits for defined Quebec temporary workers who had been invited under the PSTQ, submitted a DSP and met one of the policy's valid employer-specific permit, maintained-work-authorization or recently expired-permit situations. The employer and Quebec-work conditions were tied to the worker's existing permit and subsequent application.
transition_rule: The policy was replaced on June 5, 2026. Applications pending on June 5 were expressly brought under the successor policy, which also added spouse/common-law-partner facilitation.

topic: Quebec PSTQ prospective permanent residence work-permit public policy
date_basis: The signed A25.2 public policy takes effect upon signature, is dated June 5, 2026 and expires December 31, 2026 unless revoked earlier.
previous_rule: This policy expressly revokes and replaces the temporary Quebec PSTQ work-permit public policy signed March 12, 2026 and effective March 13, 2026.
new_rule: The policy facilitates employer-specific work permits for defined Quebec temporary workers invited under the PSTQ who submitted a DSP and meet one of the policy's valid-permit, maintained-work-authorization or recently expired-permit situations. It also facilitates open work permits for qualifying spouses or common-law partners who are accompanying family members and meet the stated temporary-status or restoration conditions.
transition_rule: The policy applies to applications received on or after June 5, 2026 and to applications pending on that date, including those pending under the March 12 predecessor. It contains distinct exemptions for the valid/maintained-status, expired/restoration and spouse cohorts; it is not a general Quebec open-work-permit measure.

topic: Francophone Minority Communities Student Pilot study-permit public policy
date_basis: The archived policy took effect upon signature and is dated September 18, 2025. The June 25, 2026 updated policy expressly revokes and replaces it, so this archive bounds the predecessor's active state through June 24, 2026.
previous_rule: The September 18, 2025 policy itself replaced the original FMCSP study-permit public policy signed August 13, 2024; that original policy is not yet separately archived here.
new_rule: The 2025 FMCSP study public policy facilitated study permits for qualifying French-speaking applicants from specified countries/regions to participating postsecondary DLIs outside Quebec, required primarily French study in a full-time program of at least two years leading to a degree or diploma, and provided related family facilitation. It set annual Part A intake caps of 2,300 for August 26, 2024-August 25, 2025 and 2,970 for August 26, 2025-August 25, 2026.
transition_rule: Pending applications under the original August 2024 policy were to be processed under this September 2025 replacement. The policy was in turn replaced by the June 25, 2026 updated FMCSP study-permit policy.

topic: Updated Francophone Minority Communities Student Pilot study-permit public policy
date_basis: The updated policy takes effect upon signature and is dated June 25, 2026. Part A expires August 25, 2027; Parts B and C remain until the linked FMCSP permanent-residence/open-work-permit policy expires November 30, 2032, unless revoked earlier.
previous_rule: This policy expressly revokes and replaces the FMCSP study-permit public policy signed September 18, 2025.
new_rule: The updated FMCSP study-permit policy continues a facilitated study-permit pathway for qualifying French-speaking applicants from specified countries/regions to eligible participating DLIs outside Quebec. Part A requires an FMCSP study-permit application before entry, citizenship within the specified OIF-country group, and an eligible French-taught postsecondary program meeting the policy's duration and credential conditions. The policy also contains family-member facilitation parts.
transition_rule: Part A is capped at 2,970 accepted study-permit applications for August 26, 2025-August 25, 2026 and 2,970 for August 26, 2026-August 25, 2027. Applications received under the prior FMCSP policy between August 26, 2025 and the June 25, 2026 effective date count toward the first of those caps. Different parts have different expiry dates, so no single effective_to date is asserted for the whole policy.

topic: FMCSP permanent-residence and open-work-permit public policy
date_basis: The archived policy took effect upon signature and is dated September 18, 2025. The June 25, 2026 updated policy expressly revokes and replaces it. The archived page also prints the impossible calendar date 'November 31, 2031' as its nominal expiry; this archive does not normalize that source typo and instead bounds the historical active state by the verified June 25, 2026 replacement.
previous_rule: The September 18, 2025 policy itself replaced an FMCSP permanent-residence policy signed October 3, 2024; that earlier policy is not yet separately archived here.
new_rule: The 2025 policy facilitated permanent residence for qualifying FMCSP graduates outside Quebec and open work permits for qualifying principal applicants awaiting a PR decision. It also contained facilitation for accompanying family members, including open-work-permit pathways of up to three years in specified circumstances.
transition_rule: Applications received while this policy was in force were governed by its conditions. The policy was replaced by the June 25, 2026 updated FMCSP PR/open-work-permit public policy; this archive preserves the official source's impossible nominal expiry text as a source-quality note rather than silently correcting it.

topic: Updated FMCSP permanent-residence and open-work-permit public policy
date_basis: The updated public policy takes effect upon signature, is dated June 25, 2026 and expires November 30, 2032 unless revoked earlier.
previous_rule: This policy expressly revokes and replaces the FMCSP permanent-residence public policy signed September 18, 2025.
new_rule: The policy creates permanent-residence facilitation for qualifying in-Canada FMCSP graduates outside Quebec and open-work-permit facilitation while a qualifying PR application is pending. Principal applicants must have held an FMCSP study permit and completed the required full-time French-taught program of at least two years leading to a degree or diploma at a participating DLI, together with the policy's status, residence and evidence conditions.
transition_rule: A qualifying principal applicant with valid status or eligible restoration may request an open work permit or renewal for up to three years while the Part 1 PR application is pending, with credential/completion evidence. Accompanying family members may qualify for specified work/study/TRV/status facilitation under Part 5. The policy applies only to applications received from June 25, 2026 through expiry or earlier revocation.

topic: Visitor in-Canada work-permit temporary public policy
date_basis: IRCC's August 28, 2024 notice states the temporary public policy ended effective immediately that day.
previous_rule: Since August 2020, qualifying visitors in Canada could use the temporary public policy to apply for a work permit from inside Canada without first leaving. Certain former work-permit holders who had changed to visitor status could also request interim work authorization while a new work-permit application was processed.
new_rule: IRCC ended the visitor in-Canada work-permit temporary public policy effective August 28, 2024. New applicants could no longer rely on that policy to bypass the ordinary restrictions on applying for a work permit from inside Canada.
transition_rule: IRCC states that applications submitted before August 28, 2024 under the temporary public policy continue to be processed under it.

authority: Government of Ontario, Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program
topic: OINP redesign procedural framework
date_basis: O. Reg. 47/26 was filed March 16, 2026. Section 8(2) makes the specified redesign provisions effective on the later of filing and May 30, 2026; OINP's May 29 update confirms implementation on May 30.
previous_rule: O. Reg. 421/17 previously contained a fixed list of nomination categories and category-specific expression-of-interest and Express Entry process wording.
new_rule: Effective May 30, 2026, O. Reg. 47/26 removed the fixed category provisions and generalized the expression-of-interest and notification-of-interest process for redesigned OINP categories. For job-offer-based pathways, the redesign requires a registered employer and employer-submitted job offer before employment-position approval.
transition_rule: OINP states that applications already received under the existing framework are assessed under the eligibility requirements in place at the time of application.

authority: Government of Ontario, Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program
topic: Ontario Workforce Priority stream
date_basis: OINP's June 26 update states the amendments to O. Reg. 422/17 came into force June 25, 2026. O. Reg. 204/26 was made, filed and published on e-Laws on June 25, 2026.
previous_rule: Before the redesign, OINP operated eight former streams under the prior framework, including employer job offer, graduate and Ontario Express Entry streams.
new_rule: Effective June 25, 2026, O. Reg. 204/26 removed the former eight-stream structure and created the Ontario Workforce Priority stream, with regulatory categories for TEER 0-3, TEER 4-5 and self-employed physicians and detailed applicant, employer, job-offer, work-experience, language and education criteria in O. Reg. 422/17.
transition_rule: OINP closed the former EOI system to new registrations and said no further invitations would be issued under the former streams. Uninvited former-stream EOIs and associated job offers were withdrawn during the platform update. Applications already submitted after an invitation under a former stream continue to be assessed under the requirements in force when submitted. Employers using Workforce Priority must submit a new job offer and employment-position approval application through the redesigned process.

authority: Government of Ontario, Ontario Immigrant Nominee Program
topic: Ontario Workforce Priority stream
date_basis: The official OINP August 4, 2026 program update states that the ministry opened the expression-of-interest portal for the Ontario Workforce Priority stream that day.
previous_rule: The Ontario Workforce Priority stream had been created by the June 25 regulatory amendments, but the redesigned expression-of-interest portal was not yet open during the implementation transition.
new_rule: On August 4, 2026, OINP opened the expression-of-interest portal for the Ontario Workforce Priority stream, making the redesigned stream operational for eligible TEER 0-3, TEER 4-5 and self-employed physician pathways.
transition_rule: Former-stream EOIs that did not result in an invitation were not carried forward as Workforce Priority EOIs. Eligible candidates and employers must use the redesigned stream's current employer/job-offer and EOI workflow.

topic: PGWP eligibility for public-private curriculum licensing programs
date_basis: IRCC's March 22, 2024 notice expressly moved implementation from the previously announced September 1, 2024 date to May 15, 2024 and states that students who begin this type of program on May 15, 2024 or later are not PGWP-eligible when they graduate.
previous_rule: IRCC had announced on January 22, 2024 that graduates of college programs delivered through public-private curriculum licensing arrangements would become ineligible for PGWPs starting September 1, 2024. The March 22 notice advanced that implementation date.
new_rule: Students who begin an applicable college program delivered through a public-private curriculum licensing arrangement on May 15, 2024 or later are not eligible for a post-graduation work permit on graduation.
transition_rule: The May 15 start-date threshold is program-start based. IRCC's current curriculum-licensing and PGWP pages preserve the protected treatment for students who began before the applicable threshold and otherwise meet PGWP requirements. This event does not reconstruct the distinct earlier rule for certain inter-provincial curriculum-licensing arrangements.

authority: Governor in Council / Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
topic: Off-campus work hours for eligible international students
date_basis: SOR/2024-219 was registered November 8, 2024 and states that the Regulations come into force on registration. It replaced IRPR 186(v)(iii) with a 24-hours-per-week maximum during a regular academic session.
previous_rule: IRPR 186(v)(iii) ordinarily limited eligible study permit holders to 20 hours per week of off-campus work during regular academic sessions. A separate temporary public policy had temporarily lifted that limit for defined cohorts but expired April 30, 2024.
new_rule: Effective November 8, 2024, eligible international students may work off campus without a work permit for no more than 24 hours per week during a regular academic session under R186(v)(iii), while qualifying students may continue to work full-time during regularly scheduled breaks.
transition_rule: The regulatory 24-hour limit applies from November 8, 2024. IRCC's current operational page states that a study permit still printed with a 20-hour condition does not prevent an otherwise eligible student from working up to the current 24-hour regulatory maximum.

authority: Governor in Council / Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
topic: Study permit requirement when changing post-secondary DLI
date_basis: SOR/2024-219 was registered November 8, 2024 and came into force on registration. New IRPR 217.1 requires a study permit holder in Canada whose permit names a DLI to submit a new study permit application naming a different DLI before attending that new institution.
previous_rule: Before the November 8, 2024 amendments, post-secondary students could change DLIs under the prior framework without a new study permit naming the new institution, although IRCC required students to update their DLI information.
new_rule: From November 8, 2024, an in-Canada study permit holder whose permit names a DLI and who intends to attend a different DLI must submit a new study permit application naming the new DLI. The amendments also tie the study-permit enrolment condition to the DLI named on the permit and add a permit-invalidity consequence when the holder is no longer enrolled there other than because studies were completed.
transition_rule: IRPR 189.1 permits study at the new DLI while the new study-permit application is pending only where the student has remained in Canada since receiving the new LOA, continues to comply with the previous permit conditions other than enrolment at the old DLI, and the former DLI closed, discontinued the program, was placed on the suspension list or lost designated status. Later operational requirements, including PAL/TAL rules where applicable, must be checked separately.

authority: Governor in Council / Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
topic: PNP federal-provincial eligibility assessment roles under IRPR 87
date_basis: SOR/2026-63 was registered March 30, 2026 and section 2 states that the Regulations come into force on registration. The Regulatory Impact Analysis Statement expressly says the amendments apply to new cases and to existing PNP inventory for which an eligibility decision has not been rendered.
previous_rule: Under the previous IRPR 87 framework, provincial/territorial and federal processing duplicated assessment of the nominee's ability to become economically established and intent to reside, and IRCC retained authority to substitute its own evaluation of economic establishment in specified circumstances.
new_rule: Effective March 30, 2026, IRPR 87(2)-(3) requires a valid nomination under an in-force PNP agreement, selection criteria approved in writing by the Minister, and nomination based on economic-establishment ability and intent to reside. The nominating province or territory has sole responsibility to evaluate those two criteria. IRCC's assessment focuses on confirming prescribed PNP eligibility/nomination requirements and federal admissibility rather than duplicating those provincial evaluations.
transition_rule: The amendments apply both to applications submitted after March 30, 2026 and to existing PNP inventory where an eligibility decision had not yet been rendered. The source expressly states that IRCC would communicate this inventory treatment through updated operational instructions. IRCC retains admissibility and program-integrity functions; this event does not imply that nomination eliminates all federal review.

topic: Post-secondary student work placements without a separate co-op work permit
date_basis: IRCC's April 9, 2026 notice and current student-work-placement instructions expressly state that, as of April 1, 2026, eligible post-secondary international students no longer need a separate co-op work permit for required student work placements.
previous_rule: Before April 1, 2026, international students generally needed a co-op work permit when a required work placement formed an essential part of the academic, professional or vocational program, subject to the then-applicable eligibility rules.
new_rule: As of April 1, 2026, eligible post-secondary international students do not need a separate co-op work permit for required co-op or internship placements. The placement must form part of the program and the student must meet IRCC's current student-work-placement eligibility conditions. Secondary-school students still require a co-op work permit.
transition_rule: Existing valid co-op work permits may be used for their full validity. IRCC's April 9 notice states that eligible active pending post-secondary co-op work-permit applications will be withdrawn. This exemption does not remove the study-permit, DLI, program, placement-percentage or other eligibility conditions on the current IRCC instructions.

topic: Post-graduation work permit duration for master's degree graduates
date_basis: IRCC's February 5, 2024 reform notice states that starting February 15, 2024 a three-year PGWP would be available to eligible graduates of master's degree programs shorter than two years. IRCC's current PGWP duration page states the same February 15, 2024 threshold.
previous_rule: For an eligible program of at least eight months but less than two years, PGWP duration was generally limited to up to the length of the study program; a master's degree shorter than two years did not by itself provide a three-year PGWP duration rule.
new_rule: As of February 15, 2024, an eligible graduate of a master's degree program can qualify for a three-year PGWP even when the master's program was less than two years, provided the program was at least eight months (900 hours for Quebec programs) and the applicant meets the other PGWP eligibility requirements. The special duration rule does not apply to certificate or diploma programs.
transition_rule: The official sources state the special master's-duration rule starts February 15, 2024. This archive does not infer a different filing-date transition for applications before that threshold where the cited sources do not state one.

topic: Family open work permits for spouses of international students
date_basis: IRCC's February 5, 2024 reform notice announced the coming restriction. Official IRCC Question Period records later state that IRCC implemented the restriction on March 19, 2024. The rule state is bounded through January 20, 2025 because IRCC expressly made the successor family-OWP restrictions effective January 21, 2025.
previous_rule: Before March 19, 2024, family open-work-permit eligibility for spouses and common-law partners of international students was broader and was not limited to the graduate/professional/pilot cohorts identified by the March 19 restriction.
new_rule: From March 19, 2024, open work permit eligibility under the international-student spouse measure was restricted to spouses and common-law partners of students in master's and doctoral degree programs, certain professional degree programs and select eligible pilot programs.
transition_rule: IRCC's February 5 notice stated that spouses and common-law partners seeking to extend an existing open work permit would continue to be eligible under the stream once the restriction took effect. On January 21, 2025, a successor rule further narrowed the master's cohort to programs of at least 16 months and set the current specified-program framework.

topic: PGWP applications at ports of entry
date_basis: IRCC's June 21, 2024 news release states that foreign nationals can no longer apply for a PGWP at the border, effective immediately. Current IRCC work-permit instructions state that as of June 21, 2024 a PGWP cannot be applied for at a port of entry.
previous_rule: Before June 21, 2024, an otherwise eligible foreign national could in some circumstances seek a PGWP at a port of entry, including through the practice commonly called flagpoling.
new_rule: As of June 21, 2024, foreign nationals can no longer apply for a post-graduation work permit at a port of entry, whether at an airport, land border or marine border when entering Canada.
transition_rule: The restriction took effect immediately on June 21, 2024. It is specific to PGWP filing at ports of entry and is preserved separately from the broader December 23, 2024 termination of work- and study-permit flagpoling.

authority: Government of Canada / Canada Border Services Agency
topic: Work and study permit flagpoling at ports of entry
date_basis: The Canada Border Services Agency's December 23, 2024 release states that work and study permits would no longer be provided to flagpolers at ports of entry effective December 23, 2024 at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time.
previous_rule: Before the December 23, 2024 cutoff, some temporary residents in Canada could leave and re-enter Canada to request work- or study-permit service at a port of entry if they were otherwise eligible. PGWP applications had already been separately barred from ports of entry on June 21, 2024.
new_rule: Effective December 23, 2024 at 11:59 p.m. ET, work and study permits are generally no longer provided at ports of entry to foreign nationals who flagpole. Applications and renewals are to be submitted through IRCC unless a listed exemption applies.
transition_rule: CBSA listed limited exemptions, including U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents; specified professionals and technicians under listed free-trade agreements; certain spouses/common-law partners under specified agreements; qualifying international truck drivers with maintained status after a timely renewal; and people with a pre-existing CBSA permit-processing appointment.

topic: Provincial or territorial attestation letter requirement for study permits
date_basis: IRCC's February 5, 2024 clarification states that as of 8:30 a.m. ET on January 22, 2024 most new post-secondary students at the college or undergraduate level had to include a provincial attestation letter. MI75 later expressly identifies the Ministerial Instructions it amended as having taken effect January 22, 2024.
previous_rule: Before the January 22, 2024 intake-control measure, there was no general federal PAL/TAL requirement requiring most affected study permit applicants to obtain a provincial or territorial allocation attestation before filing.
new_rule: From 8:30 a.m. ET on January 22, 2024, most new post-secondary study permit applicants at the college or undergraduate level, and most non-degree graduate-program applicants, had to include a provincial attestation letter from the province or territory where they intended to study unless an exemption applied.
transition_rule: IRCC stated that applications received before 8:30 a.m. ET on January 22, 2024 and already-approved study permits required no action. Under the 2024 rule state, master's and doctoral degree students, primary and secondary students, in-Canada study/work permit holders including study-permit extensions, in-Canada family members of permit holders, and specified visiting/exchange students were among the exempt cohorts. Later instructions changed the scope.

topic: PAL/TAL requirement expanded to graduate students and additional in-Canada applicants
date_basis: IRCC announced on September 18, 2024 that master's and doctoral students would be included in the 2025 study-permit cap and would have to submit a PAL/TAL. IRCC's January 24, 2025 allocation notice confirms the requirement extended to master's and doctoral students and most applicants applying from inside Canada; current IRCC instructions identify January 22, 2025 as the operative date for the 2025 PAL/TAL changes. A later January 1, 2026 exemption only superseded the public-DLI master's/doctoral component, so no record-level effective_to date is asserted for the broader 2025 expansion.
previous_rule: Under the 2024 PAL/TAL framework, master's and doctoral degree students and several in-Canada cohorts were exempt from the attestation requirement.
new_rule: For the 2025 cap year, the PAL/TAL requirement expanded to master's and doctoral degree students and most applicants applying from within Canada. Existing study permit holders applying to extend at the same DLI and same level remained exempt, along with specified other exempt cohorts.
transition_rule: The change was announced September 18, 2024 for 2025 implementation. A new PAL/TAL was required in most cases when changing schools or levels from January 22, 2025. On January 1, 2026, degree-granting master's and doctoral students at public DLIs became exempt again; that successor only supersedes the public-DLI graduate component, not the PAL/TAL framework as a whole.

topic: PAL/TAL exemption for public-DLI master's and doctoral degree students
date_basis: IRCC's November 25, 2025 notice expressly states that as of January 1, 2026 master's and doctoral level students enrolled at a public DLI will not need a PAL/TAL. Current IRCC PAL/TAL and graduate-student instructions preserve the same January 1, 2026 threshold.
previous_rule: During the 2025 cap year, master's and doctoral degree students were included among PAL/TAL-required cohorts, subject to the applicable exemptions then in force.
new_rule: As of January 1, 2026, students applying for a degree-granting master's or doctoral program at a public designated learning institution do not need to submit a PAL/TAL with the study permit application. Other applicants remain subject to the current PAL/TAL framework unless another exemption applies.
transition_rule: The exemption applies from January 1, 2026 and is limited to degree-granting master's and doctoral programs at public DLIs. It does not create a general graduate-program exemption. Applicants studying in Quebec must still meet Quebec requirements, including CAQ requirements where applicable.
